To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The government of Taiwan has neither made the most use of technology to incorporate citizens’ needs in e-government nor made necessary changes in the institutional arrangements for integrated service delivery; (2) The problems and challenges of enhancing e-government in Taiwan include the narrow-mindedness of the IT personnel in charge and a risk-averse organizational culture amongst public servants; (3) Transforming the role of IT staff, strengthening political leadership, and developing strong public values are the necessary measures to enhance e-government
